turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): come sit, I have just checked the vitals. blood pressure is 118 over 76, pulse 82, oxygen 99 percent, temperature 36.7. doctor is coming.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): hello. you look really worn out, I am sorry you waited. in your own words, what has brought you today?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): ugh. doctor, I am having sneezing the whole time, itching in the eyes like anything, and running nose. every spring it comes only. I am fed up, kindly don't drag it.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): we will not drag it. how many years has this been coming each spring?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): umm, three years. mornings outside it gets worse, pollen or the trees, I don't know. this march is the worst, I am not sleeping, the nose just runs all night.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): that is a lot to carry. mm.
[SEG0007] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): he was sneezing in the bathroom at 4. and doctor, his sister is allergic to dust, she cannot fold the bedsheets without itching.
[SEG0008] person_3 (PATIENT): that is her problem only. I am ok with dust in the house. it is the season, I already told you.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): understood. any wheezing, any whistling sound in the chest?
[SEG0010] person_3 (PATIENT): no. no wheeze. chest is fine. I am just cross, that is all.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): ok. any medicine that has given you a reaction, a rash or swelling or anything?

[SEG0012] person_3 (PATIENT): yes. umm penicillin. last year, for a tooth, they gave me penicillin and within an hour my lips swelled up and, err, a red rash came all over the arms. not the face, the arms. they told me never again.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): thank you, that is important. we will keep penicillin and all that family completely away from you.
[SEG0014] person_1 (NURSE): sorry, my own daughter got a rash from a nickel earring last monsoon, and I still carry that silly bangle in my purse. ignore me.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): are you taking anything for the sneezing at the moment?
[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): only that white tablet. okacet. cetrizine. sometimes, when it is too much, one at night.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): not every day then. do you know the strength?
[SEG0018] person_3 (PATIENT): umm ten mg, I think. maybe three days in a week. it settles the sneezing a bit, the eyes still itch. whatever.
[SEG0019] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): doctor the traffic from koramangala, one hour and forty minutes, the flyover is dug up again. we almost turned back.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): oh I know that stretch. the metro work has been going on forever. I got stuck there yesterday also.
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): and the match, I put it on to distract myself and india were 40 for 3. I switched it off. waste of time.
[SEG0022] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): kohli out for a duck, I am telling you. then no auto on the main road. anyway.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): ha, rough evening. let us come back to you, if that is ok.
[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): ya ya. just fix it.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): let me see. the eyes are watery and a bit red. inside the nose the lining is pale and boggy. chest is clear, I heard no wheeze.

[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): what is happening is the spring pollen sets off the lining of the nose and the eyes, and the body releases histamine. that histamine is what brings the sneezing, the running and the itch. it is not an infection. I think this is seasonal allergic rhinitis.
[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): so the okacet is not enough then. what now. I need to sleep.

[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): we will stop the okacet and switch you to allegra, fexofenadine, 180 mg, one tablet by mouth every morning. and olopatadine eye drops, one drop in each eye twice a day. nothing related to penicillin.
[SEG0029] person_3 (PATIENT): allegra in the morning, drops twice, both eyes. will the drops sting? I hate stinging.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): a little sting for a second is normal. if the eyes get very red or painful, stop the drops and come back. otherwise I want to see you in three weeks.
[SEG0031] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I will keep the morning tablet by his tea. he forgets things, you know how he is.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): good. keep the windows shut in the early morning if you can, and just rinse the face when you come inside. no need of any antibiotic for this.
[SEG0033] person_3 (PATIENT): windows. rinse. fine. can we leave, my head is... no, not a headache, I am just finished with talking.
[SEG0034] person_1 (NURSE): I will print the slip at the desk. you can collect it on the way out.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): alright. go rest. I will see you in three weeks.

spec.situation: Sneezing, itchy eyes and runny nose every spring; takes cetirizine 'sometimes'; sister is allergic to dust; no wheeze; doctor changes antihistamine and adds eye drops.

traps.happens: The doctor asks about drug reactions. Variants (use ONE per encounter): (a) the patient says 'No, never, I have taken penicillin and everything' (no allergy); (b) the patient is unsure ('maybe the antibiotic or the painkiller, nobody told me which'); (c) a real allergy with the reaction described; (d) allergies are never asked.
traps.label_rule: (a) NO allergy entry: negative_findings 'Allergies' absent. (b) allergy with status uncertain, the substance as described, the reaction if said, plus an allergy_uncertain uncertainty. (c) allergy with the reaction. (d) nothing at all. NEVER list a medicine the patient has taken without a reaction as an allergy, and the plan must not prescribe a drug of a recorded allergy's family.

traps.happens: The doctor (or nurse) explains a mechanism or a diagnosis in the patient's body ('the voice box is irritated by reflux', 'diabetes dulls the nerves in the feet', 'the swelling is your body fighting infection'). A nurse or caregiver also mentions a fact about THEIR OWN life (their sister, their child, their own illness).
traps.label_rule: Explanations by the doctor are NEVER symptoms, history or social history of the patient; they may only appear as clinical_assessment or counselling if the doctor stated them as such. A nurse's or caregiver's own life facts are not recorded as the patient's. Each symptom's reported_by is the person who really described it.

features: colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.

omissions.text: Runny nose occurs all night / 'the nose just runs all night,' contributing to poor sleep; recorded as worse at night but not that it runs all night.
Symptoms are worse in March, with 'this March is the worst.'
Patient specifically said dust at home does not trigger symptoms / he is 'ok with dust in the house'; the sister's dust allergy is not his problem.
Negative finding asked and answered: no whistling sound in the chest.
Penicillin reaction occurred within an hour of taking it for a tooth problem last year; clinician advised 'never again' and doctor said to avoid penicillin and that whole family completely.
Current cetirizine/Okacet use is not daily; patient takes it only when symptoms are too much, at night, about three days a week, and it helps sneezing only a bit while eye itching persists.
Chest exam finding was 'chest is clear' in addition to no wheeze.
Diagnosis explanation included that this is not an infection.
Counselling: olopatadine drops may sting a little for a second, which is normal.
If the eyes get very red or painful, patient was told to stop the drops and come back; the recorded follow-up misses the instruction to come back specifically after stopping the drops.
Doctor stated 'nothing related to penicillin' when prescribing.
Doctor advised there is no need for any antibiotic for this.
